text: {"score":3,"justification":"The core numbers match the card (24.1%, 3.4%, 5.91, 2.95, 37%, 44 docs, 19 99215 docs, 1 below, 7 of 36). The summary is cautious and its next steps are concrete. But several claims are unsupported or wrong, and the narrative is internally inconsistent. The headline says charts 'largely support' billed levels, while the body calls the pattern 'consistent with upcoding'. It also asserts that the share runs 'several times the all-provider rate in every complexity band', and the card does not bear that out. An investigator would have to recheck parts of it.","problems":["The 'every complexity band' claim is wrong: the 3-condition band is 15.4% vs 8.8% (about 1.7x) and the 4-condition band is 33.3% vs 15% (about 2.2x). Neither is 'several times'.","The summary says C0092011 and C0091944 were 'flagged', but nothing on the card flags them. C0092011 is only a low-complexity 99215 claim, and C0091944 is another one.","The comparison rate is described as 'against 15% for the comparison providers'. The card gives the all-provider rate at 99215 as 0.147, which is acceptable, but the summary frames it as an 'unsupported rate' without saying so clearly.","The numbers 16 and 32 (data and problems shares) are not on the card. They come from note-check tool output that is not visible here, so they cannot be verified.","Claims about 'duplicate-note signals' and 'templated' notes lack visible support; the listed note-check shares do not mention duplicates.","The headline says charts largely support billing, but the rationale says the pattern is 'consistent with upcoding', which makes the lean muddled.","Cited C0091952 is a 99215 for back pain, but the summary's text on simple problems cites C0091972 and C0091987 without including them in the cited ids; C0092165 is described as found below the billed level without noting its minutes are unrecorded as a limitation.","The documentation covers only 18% of claims; this is noted, but the summary does not flag that the 99215 documented sample (19 of 59) is the sole basis for the 'supported' finding."]}
